contract.method: GET / POST / DELETE; WebSocket remote progress
contract.url: configured companionUrl (defaults rootContext+/companion), provider drive/dropbox/onedrive login/list/get/mutation paths; returned websocket URL
contract.request: Provider query/auth metadata and remote file transfer body {protocol,endpoint,headers,metadata,...}; provider authentication adds uppy-auth-token.
contract.headersCsrf: Initial companionHeaders contains only X-CSRF-Token from existing getter. Delayed config calls existing provider.setCompanionHeaders, which updates RequestClient private header storage. Tus custom headers are not copied outward.
contract.response: Provider list/auth/remote token consumed by installed Uppy; upload socket drives completion/progress. Outer POST/DELETE must pass native apiProtect.
contract.status: A/P2 confirmed and fixed; angular-companion-results.json executes actual installed RequestClient with real native CSRF/session HTTP. Provider dispatch controlled; no live OAuth/cloud transfer claimed.
contract.server: packages/redbox-core/src/http/express/companion.ts

outsideProjects: Shared sails-ng-common is imported by Angular and its browser markdown-parser.browser.ts has one bundled marked import. Other tracked Angular/HttpClient imports outside projects are developer generators or test/qualification harnesses. No outside HttpClient API callsites.
limitations: External institution URLs, dynamic server-supplied templates/configuration and transitive library implementation requests are described by their concrete initiator/protocol. No finite list can enumerate arbitrary deployment values.
Literal imports can share one emitted chunk; counts refer to source callsites, not a promised chunk count.
Parent owns root assets/EJS and final build/static/page qualification. No claim of cloud credentials/OAuth or every external provider being contacted.
